title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, drawing a parallel to the present generation's rejection of God's gifts. He emphasizes that the same Holy Spirit works today through signs and wonders, and those who reject it will be condemned by the Queen of Sheba at the judgment.

title: The Called-Out
summary: William Branham preaches on the imminent judgment of God and the need for the Church to separate from the world, using the examples of Noah and Lot. He emphasizes that before judgment falls, God sends a message of mercy and calls His people out, just as He is doing in the present day through supernatural signs and the revelation of Christ.

title: The Mighty Conqueror
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus Christ as the ultimate conqueror over sin, death, and hell, contrasting worldly conquerors like Hitler and Napoleon. He shares a personal story of being lost in the Adirondack mountains and being guided by God, and calls for surrender to Christ.

title: His Wonders to Perform
summary: William Branham speaks on the mysterious ways of God, using the visit of the Magi to the infant Jesus as a central illustration. He emphasizes that God works all things together for good, leads by His light, and calls believers to walk in faith and obedience.

title: The Queen of the South
summary: William Branham speaks on the Queen of Sheba as a type of the believer who seeks God despite obstacles, contrasting her faith with the unbelief of the religious leaders of Jesus' day. He emphasizes the importance of recognizing the supernatural work of the Holy Spirit and warns against blasphemy against the Holy Ghost.
themes: The Queen of Sheba as a type of believer
The importance of hearing the Word

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing the need to hear Christ above all else. He contrasts the law (Moses) and justice (Elijah) with the mercy and salvation found in Jesus, urging believers to be genuine and obedient. The sermon calls for a real display of Christ's love through the Holy Spirit in the last days.

title: Jehovah-jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the redemptive name Jehovah-jireh, using the story of Abraham and Isaac to illustrate God's provision of a sacrifice. He emphasizes faith in God's promises and the importance of separation from unbelief, drawing parallels to the present-day work of the Holy Spirit.

title: The Oneness of Unity
summary: William Branham preaches on the unity of believers under God's Spirit versus the devil's attempts to unite people under man-made systems. He contrasts the Tower of Babel with Pentecost, emphasizing the need to be filled with the Holy Spirit after repentance. The sermon calls for heroism in faith, using the story of Arnold von Winkelried as an illustration.

title: The Handwriting On The Wall
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Belshazzar's feast and the handwriting on the wall, drawing parallels to modern America's moral decay, reliance on military might, and rejection of the supernatural. He warns of impending judgment and calls for repentance.

title: Escape Hither, Come Quickly
summary: William Branham preaches on the urgency of escaping judgment by heeding the Holy Spirit's warning, drawing parallels between the days of Noah and Lot and the present time. He emphasizes that God always sends supernatural signs before judgment and calls believers to come out of worldly systems into Christ.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham speaks on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses divine healing, the role of the Holy Spirit in the church, and the signs of the Messiah as seen in the Gospels, urging believers to recognize Christ's presence and power in the current age.

title: The Queen of the South
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, drawing parallels to the present generation's need to seek God's supernatural gifts. He emphasizes the importance of personal faith, the danger of unbelief, and the manifestation of Christ through the Holy Spirit.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Transfiguration, emphasizing that believers must hear and obey Christ alone, not the law or prophets. He calls the church to holiness and separation from worldliness, warning against denominationalism and compromise.

title: The Door Inside The Door
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Christ knocks at the heart's door but only the individual can open it. He explores various 'inner doors' such as selfishness, pride, and faith, urging believers to let Christ be not only Saviour but also Lord and Ruler of every aspect of their lives.
themes: the importance of receiving God's promise

title: God's Eye
summary: William Branham preaches on God's guiding eye, referencing Psalm 32:7-8 and John 5:19. He explains that Jesus looked through God's eye to perceive thoughts and heal, and that the same Holy Spirit guides the Church today. The sermon includes a prayer line where Branham demonstrates the gift of discernment, revealing specific conditions and needs of individuals.

title: Thy Lovingkindness
summary: William Branham preaches on Psalm 63:1-3, emphasizing that true life is found only in God, not in worldly pleasures. He calls for repentance and a return to holy living, warning against the deceptions of sin and the coming judgment.

title: The Great Commission
summary: William Branham speaks to a gathering of ministers about the importance of unity among believers, emphasizing that the Great Commission is still relevant today. He shares personal experiences from his travels, including a vision that led him to Africa, and stresses the need for love and cooperation across denominational lines.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Transfiguration, emphasizing that God's voice from the cloud commanded 'Hear ye Him,' condemning denominational division and calling the church to genuine love and unity in Christ. He illustrates this with a story of a mother deer's sacrificial love, urging believers to display authentic Christian love to the world.

title: Door To The Heart
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Christ knocks at the door of the heart but the latch is on the inside. He challenges believers to open every area of their lives—private life, pride, selfishness, faith, and spiritual vision—to let Jesus be Lord, not just Savior. He warns of impending judgment on America for its sin and spiritual blindness.

title: The Handwriting On The Wall
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Belshazzar's feast and the handwriting on the wall, drawing parallels to modern America's moral decay and spiritual apostasy. He warns of impending judgment and calls for repentance, emphasizing that only Jesus Christ can interpret the signs of the times.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And For Ever
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting, emphasizing that he represents Christ, not a denomination or healing ministry. He explains that healing comes through faith in Christ's finished work at Calvary, and that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, as demonstrated by His ministry of revealing hearts and performing miracles.

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, drawing parallels to the present generation's need to recognize and accept the Holy Spirit's work. He emphasizes the importance of standing for Christ despite opposition, and calls for a decision to follow Him.

title: Love
summary: William Branham preaches on the nature of God's love (agapao) versus human love (phileo), illustrating through stories of a stamp's value, a pardon, Arnold von Winkelried's sacrifice, a maniac's conversion, a mother opossum, and a mother deer. He calls believers to display genuine love that overcomes fear and draws others to Christ.

title: As The Eagle Stirs Her Nest And Fluttereth Over Her Young
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of an eagle to describe God's care for His people, emphasizing how God stirs the nest to prepare believers for spiritual flight. He contrasts the eagle's heavenly nature with earthbound religion, calling the church to holiness and reliance on God's Word.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting by explaining his ministry's foundation on the Bible and the supernatural confirmation of God's Word. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and demonstrates how Christ revealed Himself as Messiah through supernatural knowledge, as seen with Nathanael and the Samaritan woman, expecting the same manifestation today.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Transfiguration, emphasizing that God's Word is eternal and valuable. He calls the church to genuine holiness, rejecting worldliness and denominationalism, and urges believers to hear Jesus alone.

title: Faith By Experience
summary: William Branham preaches on the nature of faith as a substance and the importance of personal experience with God. He contrasts intellectual faith with experiential faith, using biblical examples like David, Moses, and Samson to illustrate that true faith comes from encountering God's power. He calls the church to return to the Holy Ghost and fire, and invites sinners to experience Christ's resurrection power.

title: United Under One Head
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for unity under God's headship rather than human leadership, using the Tower of Babel as a cautionary example. He contrasts head knowledge with heart faith, urging believers to be filled with the Holy Spirit and united under Christ.

title: God Keeps His Word
summary: William Branham preaches on God's faithfulness to keep His promises, using the example of Simeon who was promised he would not die before seeing the Messiah. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit leads believers to the fulfillment of God's Word, and demonstrates this through a healing service where the Spirit reveals specific conditions and needs.

title: The Mighty Conqueror
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus Christ as the ultimate conqueror over sin, death, hell, and the grave. He contrasts earthly conquerors like Napoleon with Christ's sacrificial victory at Calvary, emphasizing that believers are more than conquerors through Him. The sermon includes a call to repentance and a prayer line for healing.

title: A Missionary Talk
summary: William Branham delivers a passionate missionary talk, emphasizing the need for Holy Spirit power and signs following believers to prove the resurrection of Jesus to the world. He shares stories from his travels, including encounters with a Mohammedan woman and a British doctor, to illustrate that the Gospel must be demonstrated through supernatural works, not just words.

title: I Know My Redeemer Liveth
summary: William Branham preaches on Easter Sunday about the certainty of the resurrection and God's unshakable purpose for believers. He draws from Job 19:23-27 and other biblical examples to show that nothing can defeat God's plan, and that true faith comes from a personal encounter with the risen Christ.

title: The Evidence of the Resurrection
summary: William Branham preaches on the evidence of Christ's resurrection, focusing on the account of the two disciples on the road to Emmaus. He emphasizes that the evening light of the last days brings a manifestation of the resurrected Christ through signs and wonders, proving He is alive and the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: The Eagle Stirring Her Nest
summary: William Branham uses the metaphor of an eagle to describe the Christian life, emphasizing that believers are born as eagles, not chickens, and must rise above worldly denominations and traditions. He illustrates how God stirs the nest to prepare His children for spiritual flight, trusting in His power and grace.
themes: Eagle as symbol of the believer

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, drawing parallels to the present generation's need to seek God's gifts. He emphasizes faith over unbelief, the importance of respecting God's gifts, and the coming judgment. The sermon calls for a personal commitment to stand for Christ.

title: The Expectations
summary: William Branham preaches on the expectations of faith, using the biblical account of Simeon and Anna who recognized the Christ child in the temple. He emphasizes that God always has a witness and that believers must be led by the Holy Spirit, not by popular opinion. He also discusses the supernatural photograph of the Pillar of Fire and the importance of expecting God to fulfill His promises.

title: Have Faith In God
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of faith in God, emphasizing that faith is the substance of things hoped for and the evidence of things not seen. He uses biblical examples like David and Goliath, Moses, and Abraham to illustrate that true faith comes from personal experience with God, not from education or seminary training. He warns of coming judgment on America and calls for a return to genuine faith.

title: Life
summary: William Branham preaches on the true meaning of life, contrasting worldly pleasures with the eternal life found in God. He emphasizes that genuine life comes from a relationship with Christ, not from sin and worldly pursuits. Branham calls believers to live as separated, holy people reflecting the character of God.

title: Zacchaeus
summary: William Branham speaks at a Full Gospel Business Men's breakfast, using the story of Zacchaeus to illustrate how prayer and conviction can lead a skeptical businessman to encounter Jesus. He emphasizes the importance of emotion in religion, soul-winning at the end time, and the power of a praying spouse.

title: The Sin Of Unbelief
summary: William Branham preaches on the sin of unbelief, emphasizing that unbelief is the root of all sin. He uses the examples of the queen of Sheba and the people of Nineveh to illustrate how faith and seeking God lead to blessing, while unbelief leads to condemnation. He calls the congregation to stand for Christ and accept Him as Savior.

title: Tested Faith Produces Goods
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of genuine faith, using biblical examples like David and Goliath, Abraham, and Moses to illustrate that tested faith produces goods. He emphasizes that faith is not intellectual assent but a substance that comes from a personal experience with God, and he calls believers to display real love and faith to a watching world.

title: Life
summary: William Branham preaches on the nature of true life, contrasting worldly pleasures with the eternal life found in God. He emphasizes that God's lovingkindness is better than physical life, and calls believers to live as sons and daughters of God, separated from worldly fashions and sins.

title: The Sign Of The Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the handwriting on the wall in Daniel 5, drawing parallels between ancient Babylon and modern America. He warns of judgment due to sin, self-sufficiency, and rejection of the supernatural, urging repentance and a return to the full Gospel.

title: Jesus of Nazareth Passeth By
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that faith in Him brings healing and salvation. He encourages believers to trust in God's promises and to set their faith on the Holy Spirit rather than on denominational divisions.
themes: the power of the Holy Spirit

title: The Sign Of The Messiah
summary: William Branham preaches on the sign of the Messiah, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He argues that the same works Jesus performed to prove He was the Messiah—such as discerning thoughts and revealing secrets—must be present in the Church today through the Holy Spirit. Branham warns against relying on denominations and education, urging believers to seek a personal encounter with the living Christ.
themes: Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
The Church as the Body of Christ

title: Jesus at the Door
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Christ knocks at the door of the heart but the latch is on the inside, requiring a personal response. He challenges believers to open every area of their lives—private life, pride, faith, and spiritual vision—to Jesus as Lord, not just Saviour. Branham warns against lukewarmness and spiritual blindness in the Laodicean Church Age.
themes: Christ knocking at the heart's door

title: Time-Tested Faith
summary: William Branham preaches on the simplicity and power of faith, emphasizing that genuine faith comes from a personal experience with God. He uses biblical examples like David, Abraham, and Moses to illustrate how meeting God transforms believers and enables them to trust Him fully. Branham calls for a return to authentic Christianity marked by the Holy Spirit's power and love.

title: The Message to the Laodicean Church
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Christ is knocking at the door of every heart, but the church has become lukewarm, self-satisfied, and blind to its true condition. He calls for repentance, unity among denominations, and a return to holiness and faith in God's Word.

title: The Mighty Conqueror
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus Christ as the ultimate conqueror over sin, death, hell, and the grave. He contrasts worldly conquerors like Napoleon and Arnold von Winkelried with Christ's victory through love and sacrifice, urging the Church to live genuine, loving lives that reflect Christ's conquering power.
themes: Christ's victory over death and hell
The Church's commission to conquer through love
The importance of playing by God's rules

title: Thirsting for Life
summary: William Branham preaches on the soul's thirst for God, contrasting worldly pleasures with the true life found in Christ. He uses the example of a king's son among slaves to illustrate how believers should conduct themselves as children of God, and warns against the devil's perversion of that holy thirst.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He explores how Jesus revealed Himself to the Jews and Samaritans through discernment and prophecy, and argues that the same manifestations must occur today for the Gentiles. Branham calls believers to seek a genuine encounter with Christ beyond denominational barriers.

title: Handwriting On The Wall
summary: William Branham preaches on the handwriting on the wall from Daniel 5, drawing parallels between ancient Babylon and modern America. He warns that America's sin and rejection of God's supernatural signs will lead to judgment, just as Babylon fell. He urges the church to awaken and be ready for the coming of the Lord.

title: Can We See Jesus?
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that the same signs and wonders that Jesus performed in His earthly ministry, such as discerning thoughts and revealing secrets, are available to the Church today. He argues that divine healing is part of the atonement and that the Gentile age is closing, requiring a return to the supernatural manifestations of the early Church.

title: The Queen of the South
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, drawing parallels to the present generation's need to seek the living God and His gifts. He emphasizes the importance of approaching God with faith and sincerity, and warns against rejecting divine gifts.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of recognizing God's gifts and the danger of rejecting them, using the examples of Jonah and the Queen of Sheba. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that the Holy Spirit's work today is the same as in biblical times.

title: By Faith, Moses
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of faith, using Moses as an example of choosing by faith over worldly pleasures. He encourages believers to look beyond the visible and temporal, and to take their stand with God's people despite persecution.

title: The Placing of Deacons
subtitle: 58-0720E
summary: William Branham oversees the election of new deacons and a treasurer for the Branham Tabernacle, emphasizing the church's sovereignty and scriptural qualifications for deacons. He presents five men to the congregation, who are unanimously approved, and then offers a prayer of dedication.

title: Why Are We Not A Denomination?
summary: William Branham explains why his congregation is not a denomination, emphasizing that denominations separate believers and are not found in Scripture. He traces the origin of denominations to the Catholic Church and argues that God deals with individuals, not organizations. Using Revelation 17, he identifies the 'great whore' as a false church that persecutes saints, contrasting it with the true Bride of Christ.

title: The Baptism of the Holy Spirit
summary: William Branham teaches on the baptism of the Holy Spirit, explaining why his church is non-denominational and emphasizing that true salvation is based on predestination and the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. He contrasts this with denominational doctrines and warns against false teachings that do not align with Scripture.

title: The Serpent's Seed
summary: William Branham preaches on the origin of sin and the serpent's seed, arguing that denominations are not ordained by God and that true salvation comes through a spiritual revelation of Christ. He emphasizes the importance of baptism in Jesus' Name and the eternal security of believers predestined before the foundation of the world.

title: Lifting Him Up Out Of History
summary: William Branham speaks about the need to call upon the historical God to act in present-day crises, drawing parallels between biblical figures like Elijah, Moses, and Jesus and the current state of the world, the church, and individual lives. He encourages faith in a God who is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and expresses hope for a new ministry to begin.

title: Faith Is Our Victory
summary: William Branham preaches on faith as the victory that overcomes the world, using examples from history, the Bible, and personal testimonies. He encourages believers to have a settled faith in God's promises, not just drift through life, and calls for an operation of faith to remove doubt and sin.

title: Hear His Voice
summary: William Branham preaches on the rarity of hearing God's voice in a world filled with distractions and false teachings. Using the story of Samuel, he emphasizes the need to quiet oneself and wait on the Lord to hear His voice. He contrasts the modern church's focus on programs and denominations with the necessity of personal communion with God.

title: Church Order
summary: William Branham outlines the order and doctrine of the Branham Tabernacle, emphasizing apostolic teachings, the operation of spiritual gifts, and the authority of the pastor. He details the proper sequence of worship, including silent prayer, tongues and interpretation, testimonies, and preaching, while warning against fanaticism and disorder.

title: Watchman, What Of The Night?
summary: William Branham preaches on the role of the watchman in Isaiah 21, warning of approaching danger and the coming of the Lord. He contrasts the world's indifference with the hope of the Morning Star for believers, emphasizing the urgency of repentance and readiness for Christ's return.

title: Where Is He, King of the Jews?
summary: William Branham preaches a Christmas sermon on the wise men seeking the newborn King, emphasizing that God leads sincere seekers through signs and the Spirit, and that the church often misses God's work due to tradition. He shares testimonies of healings and calls believers to follow the Light of Christ.

title: The Unity of One God in the One Church
summary: William Branham preaches on the unity of believers in God, contrasting true spiritual unity through the Holy Spirit with false unity under man-made systems. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is the seal of God and that believers must be born again to achieve God's purpose.
themes: God's control room in the heart
